newsitem.title: GERMANY: Veba joins oil project with Mobil.
newsitem.headline: Veba joins oil project with Mobil.

text.p: German oil company Veba Oel AG said on Thursday it would join Mobil Corp in a Venezuelan oil project expected to begin producing 66,000 barrels of oil per day in 1999.

Veba Oel took a 16.7 percent share in the project, which Mobil began with Lagoven, a subsidiary of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela. The Venezuelan congress was expected to approve the deal later this spring, Veba Oel said.

Over the next five years Veba Oel would invest about $500 million per year in the project to develop an oil field in the Cerro Negro region. The company expected its share in the partnership to yield about a million tonnes of crude oil for its Ruhr Oel GmbH refinery, which is a venture with PdVSA.
The partners would make a total investment of about $2.5 billion over the next 15 years and expected the field to produce a high level of oil until at least 2030, Veba Oel said.
The partners planned to build a refinery in Jose on the Venezuelan coast.
